data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Penelope was the wife of Odysseus. Her name means 'Weaver of All'. Despite numerous suitors trying to marry her during her husband's long absence, she remained loyal and faithful. The name Penelopa carries the meaning “Weaver of All” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Penelopa usually hope their child will grow to embody weaver of all and live with faith, good character and purpose.

Today, it is considered a classic and elegant name, evoking the image of a strong, devoted and intelligent woman. The name Penelope has been given to countless girls in various cultures, particularly in the English-speaking world.
data.spiritual_significance: Penelope's name carries a deep spiritual significance, as it represents the unwavering devotion and faithfulness of a wife. In a world where infidelity and disloyalty are all too common, Penelope's story serves as a reminder of the importance of staying true to one's spouse and remaining committed even in the face of adversity. Her willingness to endure hardship and remain steadfast in her love for her husband demonstrates the power of loyalty and patience in building strong and lasting relationships.
